tonight.headline: Down 10.0 with three starters hurt. Nothing left to set
body: Achane (knee, first quarter), Coker (quad) and Jefferson (ankle) all got hurt during their games. Your 97.8 is most of what you'll get: Jefferson, the Vikings D/ST and Pineiro are in late games that are nearly over. Footballers still have Stafford (15.9 projected) tonight and Bowers finishing. ESPN gives you 5%.

There's nothing to change. Every starter is locked. Monangai plays Monday but he's on your bench, and every RB and flex slot is already locked. The work this week is Week 4: the two cards below settle Achane's and the receivers' replacements now, before the MRIs come back.

case.label: What happened
case.body: Achane's left leg gave out on a non-contact cut on his third carry. He was ruled out in the second half (CBS; Dolphins via Heavy, 15:09 ET). Coker left with a quad injury after 3 catches on 4 targets and was ruled out (The Big Lead). Jefferson hurt his right ankle in the second quarter after 2 catches for 32 yards. He was questionable to return and walked to the locker room on his own (AtoZ Sports, 17:38 ET).

case.label: The script that wins
case.body: Stafford busts at Denver and Jefferson's ankle is only precautionary, so he comes back for a late score. Both have to happen. A 10-point gap against a starting quarterback who hasn't played yet is hard to close.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Jefferson returning in the fourth quarter. That's the only live upside left on your side.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: WHEN THE WEEK ROLLS · only if Achane is ruled out or doubtful for Week 4
doFirst.title: If Achane misses Week 4: start Tuten in his RB slot
doFirst.subtitle: Not armed. Waiting on the knee. A swap, and nobody is dropped.

case.label: The knee
case.body: It was a non-contact injury: his left leg gave out planting to cut right, less than five minutes in (CBS). He walked off on his own and came back to the sideline in uniform 'in good spirits' (Melanie Collins via CBS). No MRI result has been reported. Non-contact knee injuries are the ones that turn out long, so don't plan around a quick return until Miami says so.

case.label: Why Tuten
case.body: He's your best bench back. He's Jacksonville's starter: 15 carries for 73 yards and a touchdown today, with 2 catches on 48% of snaps (Michael Florio). Trevor Lawrence threw three touchdowns in a 35-6 win. Monangai splits Chicago's backfield with Swift behind a third-string quarterback, and Kamara shares New Orleans' work with Etienne. Next week's projection makes the final call, so if Monangai or Kamara projects higher, start him instead.

case.label: The clock
case.body: Rosters unlock after Monday night. Miami's first practice report comes out Wednesday.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Achane is cleared to play Week 4. Then the card never fires. If it does fire, it's graded on the outcome: whoever starts in Achane's slot against Achane's replacement value.

doFirst.subtitle: Not armed. Two receiver injuries today. McLaurin is first in line and Boston second.

case.label: The injuries
case.body: Coker: quad, ruled out today, and Carolina gave no timeline (The Big Lead). Jefferson: right ankle, taped, questionable to return. He wasn't limping, and the trip to the locker room may have been precautionary (AtoZ Sports).

case.label: Why McLaurin
case.body: Mariota's first start went fine: McLaurin caught 6 of 9 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown in a win at Seattle (NBC). Today undercut the idea that Mariota wouldn't target him. Boston is second: the Browns ran a lot early and he was quiet, but he caught the winning two-point conversion (Yahoo; NCFootballNews).

case.label: The clock
case.body: Rosters unlock after Monday night. Carolina and Minnesota publish their first practice reports Wednesday.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Both Coker and Jefferson practise fully by Friday, and the card never fires. If it does fire, it's graded on the outcome: McLaurin against the man he replaced.

whatWentWrong.title: Three starters hurt mid-game
whatWentWrong.lead: Achane (knee), Coker (quad) and Jefferson (ankle). All were started correctly, and together they left about 45 projected points unscored.

case.label: Not a lineup miss
case.body: The lineup as set was the projection lineup and every starter was active at kickoff. No brief could have seen these injuries coming. Coker's pregame ankle issue wasn't what took him out: it was a new quad injury.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Week 4's lineup depends on three medical reports. The two cards above settle the replacements now, so Wednesday is a checklist rather than a decision.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: All three are cleared for Week 4. Then both cards stay unarmed.

whatWentWrong.sources: CBS Sports · The Big Lead · AtoZ Sports

whatWentWrong.title: The Coker-over-McLaurin flex call lost, 3.8 to 19.7
whatWentWrong.lead: Closed WRONG. The falsifier fired: Coker got 4 targets while Mariota threw McLaurin 9.

case.label: The call
case.body: On 21 Sep the brief moved Coker into the flex because Daniels' injury meant Mariota would start. The falsifier said the call was wrong if Coker drew under five targets while McLaurin drew eight or more. Coker got 4 before the quad took him out (The Big Lead). McLaurin got 9 (NBC).

case.label: The honest part
case.body: The injury cut Coker's day short, and that doesn't rescue the call. A lineup decision is graded on its outcome, and this one lost by 15.9. The theory that Mariota would starve McLaurin was wrong on its first test.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The flex slot reopens. Week 4's projection decides it, and the second card makes McLaurin the first replacement if a receiver is out.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: The Week 3 archive disagreeing with the reported target counts. The archive grades it formally on Tuesday.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: ESPN projected Pineiro 9.4 and McPherson 7.4 this week. Cincinnati lost 30-27 at Pittsburgh (Steeler Nation); Pineiro's game is still going.

case.label: Why hold
case.body: Pineiro came in on 23 Sep. The seat's seven-day churn window runs until 30 Sep.

case.label: When to act
case.body: After 30 Sep, and only if Pineiro finishes Week 3 outside the top twenty kickers while McPherson finishes top five.

worthALook.name: Lions D/ST
worthALook.lead: The D/ST comparison. Hold the Vikings.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: Both projected 7.7. The Vikings are at 12 and still playing at Tampa. Detroit faced a Jets team missing Mitchell and Mason Taylor (RotoWire).

case.label: Why hold
case.body: This is the third D/ST in a week already. There's no gap to act on.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Only on a Week 4 projection gap of two points or more, after the churn window closes.

doNotChase.name: Dalton Schultz
doNotChase.lead: The market's right about him, and he still has no place on this roster.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Nico Collins was ruled out again (hamstring, NBC 25 Sep), so Houston's targets run through Schultz.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: One TE slot, held by Likely, and a flex that only takes RB or WR. A second TE scores zero here.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Likely being ruled out. Likely had a poor day, but a 3.3 is no reason to replace him.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: Pitts 1.5 against Likely 3.3 this week. It's the first of the three weeks in the Pitts-risk thesis, and Likely won it.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Same structural reason as Schultz: one TE slot, and the flex takes only RB or WR.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Likely being ruled out, or Pitts outscoring Likely in two of the next three weeks.

waiverAnalysis.summary: Nothing on the wire beats this roster on usage. Monangai (RB) and Boston (WR) are the weakest players you could move, and nobody on the wire clears either. That's two weeks of data, which is thin. Achane's knee could change the RB question by Tuesday, so that run should re-check it.
